notes: Open on the concentration point, not on scale alone. Point to the four rank-1 commodities and then milk as the cross-value-chain extension. Expect the question on why incomes still lag; answer that leadership in crop mix does not remove district water, productivity, and value-capture gaps.
title: Gujarat holds India’s leading positions in cotton and groundnut and remains a top-tier producer in castor, cumin and milk, making crop mix the state’s agricultural identity
subtitle: This is not a broad-based staples story; Gujarat’s farm economy is defined by a concentrated set of nationally important commercial crops and dairy, which is why income growth now depends on how each value chain performs.

chart.annotation: Gujarat is rank 1 nationally in four signature commodities and remains rank 3 in milk, showing a distinctly commercial production mix.
chart.source: Source: DA&FW, NDDB, state agriculture profiles 2024-2025 [[src:official]]

insights.text: Gujarat ranks **1** nationally in **cotton**, **groundnut**, **castor**, and **cumin**, a concentration of leadership that few states match across both field crops and spices.
The same production identity extends beyond crops: Gujarat ranks **3** in **milk**, adding a major livestock value chain to an already commercial farm base.

This leadership pattern shows why crop mix sits at the center of the state’s agricultural identity: farmer outcomes are heavily shaped by performance in a handful of high-significance commodity systems rather than a diffuse basket of small crops.

footnote: Source: DA&FW, NDDB, state agriculture profiles 2024-2025 [[src:official]]
